artifacts.summary: 4-phase plan: red baseline + (priority := 100) declaration-site fix as one atomic batch, #guard_msgs in #synth instance pin, docstring rationale at both declaration sites, full CSLib CI gate.

memory_candidates.content: Lean 4 instance-priority collision pattern in a barrel-imported library: when two instances target the same `Decidable P` goal and both carry default priority (1000), Lean prefers the LATER-DECLARED one. If one decider is kernel-reducible (e.g. Fintype enumeration) and the other is not (e.g. WellFounded.fix-based tableau), whichever module the barrel imports last silently wins, and `decide` breaks for every downstream consumer while in-repo tests keep passing purely because they do not transitively import both modules. Diagnosis: `#synth Decidable (P ...)` with both modules in scope names the selected instance. Fix: `instance (priority := 100) instName ...` at the DECLARATION site of the non-reducible one (not a consumer-side `attribute [instance 100]`, which leaves the barrel defect intact). Priority only breaks ties among APPLICABLE instances, so the lowered instance stays the sole candidate where the other's hypotheses (e.g. `Fintype`) are unavailable. Regression guard: a `#guard_msgs in #synth` pin fails with a message naming the wrong instance, whereas the downstream `decide` failures only report stuck reduction. Generalizes to any repo where a barrel module re-exports competing instances.
